clue.text: Hamish's upset following end of referendum confusion

indicators.note: following places the rearranged name after the single letter from the vote
end of asks for the final letter of the word referendum
upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the s included

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is distressed in the muddle after a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive s counts as one of the letters that 'upset' rearranges; 'following' puts the result after the letter 'end of' takes from referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a jumble or muddle of ill-assorted things.

clue.text: One described as not of woman born? A record entered in mistake

definitions.text: One described as not of woman born?

indicators.note: entered in says the article and the record go inside the word for a mistake

parts.note: a muff is a bungled attempt, such as a dropped catch
CD, a compact disc, is a record

explanation.surface: A person of unnatural birth has a recording logged in error.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Shakespeare: the witches promise Macbeth that none of woman born shall harm him. 'entered in' puts the article and the disc inside the blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakespearean thane who kills Macbeth was 'from his mother's womb untimely ripped', a Caesarean delivery.

clue.text: Bird being abrasive to cockney when talking?

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, says the long A of paper like the I of piper, so the word is heard in that accent

parts.note: sandpaper is an abrasive, a rough sheet for rubbing wood smooth

explanation.surface: A bird is rude to a Londoner during a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abrasive' is a noun here, the rough paper used on wood. Cockney is the traditional East London accent, in which 'paper' comes out close to 'piper'; 'to cockney when talking' asks for that pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: An example of the class: a small long-billed wader of shores and mudflats.

clue.text: Inventor of polo having centre of mint used up

parts.note: Marco is the first name that goes with Polo, the Venetian traveller

indicators.note: in a down clue, used up means the two picked letters are written going upwards
centre of takes the two middle letters of the word mint

explanation.surface: The creator of the mint with a hole has eaten its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is a British mint with a hole in its centre, but here 'polo' points to the traveller Marco Polo. 'centre of' takes IN from mint and 'used up' turns it into NI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian pioneer of wireless telegraphy is a famous example of one.

clue.text: Piercing cry rocks church

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: A shrill scream shakes a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' reads as a verb, shakes, but it is a noun: the loose stones on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a harsh, high-pitched shriek.

clue.text: Cheat out of money for coat

definitions.meaning: to swindle someone, typically by overcharging them
a sheep's woolly covering, or a jacket of soft warm fabric

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to swindle or overcharge; as a noun it is a sheep's wool or a warm jacket.

clue.text: One wanting trout, perhaps if freshly prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fancies trout, provided it has just been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the nine letters of IF FRESHLY. The trout looks like a dinner order; it is the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler casting an artificial insect as a lure is typically after trout or salmon.

clue.text: No more can court go after former partner

indicators.note: go after places the can and the court behind the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a tin is a can, a metal food container
CT is an abbreviation for court, as in addresses

explanation.surface: The court is no longer able to pursue someone's ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb, is able to, but it is the metal container, which 'go after' sends behind the former partner along with the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has died out exists no longer, an adjectival sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Big-leaved tree — about time mountain ash is cut right back

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: cut right back means pruned as hard as possible, leaving only the opening letter of ash

explanation.surface: It is high time the rowan was pruned hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Mountain ash is another name for the rowan, but the two words split: mountain is ALP, and 'is cut right back' prunes ash to its A.
explanation.definitionFit: An American ornamental with very large heart-shaped leaves, also called the Indian bean.

clue.text: Conservative attempt to cover up right in trouble as if in opposition

indicators.note: to cover up says the attempt wraps round the troubled piece, hiding it

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: in puts the letter for right inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A Tory bid to hide a right-winger's difficulties, seemingly while out of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is a direction here, not the political wing: 'in' drops its letter into the word for trouble, and 'to cover up' has the attempt wrap round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb for acting perversely against what is expected or wanted.

clue.text: Carry digit over ten, to begin with

indicators.note: over has the digit lying across and covering the single letter

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot

indicators.note: to begin with takes the opening letter of ten

explanation.surface: In column addition, carry a figure once the total passes ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digit' is a numeral in the sum but a toe in the wordplay; 'over' wraps it round the T that 'to begin with' takes from ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym, chiefly American: to lug something about by hand.

clue.text: Lay pine floor as sun is all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered and in disorder, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fit softwood flooring while sunshine floods the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like an instruction to fit a floor; it is the adjective meaning non-expert. 'is all over the place' rearranges the fourteen letters of PINE FLOOR AS SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, lay describes someone outside a qualified body, an amateur.

clue.text: Old pages dressed in salmon perhaps appearing dandified

indicators.note: dressed in means clothed by, so the first two pieces sit inside the fish

parts.note: a salmon is one example of a fish
PP is the abbreviation for pages in references

explanation.surface: Elderly pageboys in pink livery, looking like dandies.
explanation.walkthrough: Salmon reads as a colour of livery, but it is the fish; 'dressed in' puts O and PP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: vain and affected about clothes and appearance.

clue.text: Found heather astounding

parts.note: to found an institution is to start it
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: Someone came across heather that was amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past of find, but it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: causing sudden surprise or alarm.

clue.text: Copper rings the AA after disturbing large house

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the copper goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: after disturbing says the two words before it are used once their letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A policeman phones the breakdown service after causing trouble at a mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a roadside breakdown service, and Copper suggests a policeman. 'after disturbing' rearranges THE AA into HATEA, which the metal's symbol 'rings'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French castle or grand country residence, especially one with a vineyard.

clue.text: Reading problem tutor had after English, certainly

indicators.note: after places the word for tutor behind the other two pieces

parts.note: yes is a way of saying certainly
to tutor someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A teacher certainly had trouble with reading once the English lesson was over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tutor' is a verb here, and 'after' puts it behind E and YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching vision is a complaint that comes from too much close work with books.

clue.text: Sketch fish on harbour

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means added to the end of what is already there

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a ray is a flat-bodied sea fish

explanation.surface: Draw someone angling beside the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' reads as a verb, to angle, but it is the creature; 'on' puts it after the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to depict or describe someone in outline.

clue.text: Morse, possibly needs steer about one key name

parts.note: a steer is a young ox
on means about, as in a book on birds
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A coded message may need guidance about a single key name.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is Inspector Morse, the British fictional detective who studied and works in Oxford; the code is a decoy. 'steer' is the animal, not guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: The detective is an example of a member or graduate of the university on the Isis.

clue.text: Rapid shaking, ultimately spent, on second watch

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of spent

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a mo is a moment, a second
lo is an old exclamation meaning look, watch

explanation.surface: Trembling fast and finally exhausted during the second stint on guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second watch' looks like a sentry's shift, but the words work separately: a brief moment, then an old cry of 'look!'. 'ultimately' takes the end of spent.
explanation.definitionFit: In music it is a fast repetition or wavering of a note, a trembling effect.

clue.text: Bravery exercises bodyguard containing serious dispute

indicators.note: containing says the exercises and the bodyguard together hold the dispute inside

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercises at school
a row is a heated quarrel
the SS began as Hitler's personal bodyguard

explanation.surface: Courage tests a minder who is keeping a lid on a major quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' reads as a verb but is the school lesson; with the bodyguard it forms the outside that is 'containing' the quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in its older sense: valour or daring, especially in battle.

clue.text: One mostly attractive prize set up for a composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the whole run of pieces is written going upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: mostly means the word for attractive loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means attractive or pleasing
the last letter of nice, dropped by mostly
a cup is a trophy, a prize

explanation.surface: A largely appealing award established for someone who writes music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims NICE to NIC, and 'set up' turns the whole run I NIC CUP upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian who wrote the operas Tosca and La Bohème is an example.

clue.text: No let-up unfortunately for wealthy

indicators.note: unfortunately means things have gone badly, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sadly, the rich get no respite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the seven letters of NO LET-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: rich, especially in a lavish and showy way.

clue.text: Boy holds strong desire to be a ship's doctor

indicators.note: holds says the boy has the strong desire inside him

parts.note: a son is a boy
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A lad cherishes an ambition to become a naval medic.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical officer aboard a naval vessel traditionally has this title.

clue.text: Obvious man by bar as some drugs are sold

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
he is a pronoun for a man
a bar is the counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A conspicuous fellow at the pub, which is how some narcotics change hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at street dealing; the definition is the lawful sale of medicines by a pharmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines bought without a prescription are sold this way.

clue.text: Some crocodiles around where there are swimmers

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the run of letters is read from right to left
Some means part of the word crocodiles is taken

explanation.surface: A few crocs lurk near the bathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ODIL from inside crocodiles and 'around' turns it to face the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A public open-air pool or bathing beach, so a place for bathers.

clue.text: I will say again — as ignorant people are everywhere

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will, with the apostrophe ignored
to iterate is to say or do again

explanation.surface: A speaker repeats that the uninformed are all around.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash hides the join: the first four words are all wordplay, I'LL then ITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A looser sense than unable to read: uneducated or lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Working lad, good and performing well

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A hard-working, decent boy who is doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom, especially in sport: playing at the top of one's form.

clue.text: Use a tap catalogue to get a number sent over

parts.note: a catalogue is a list

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, so the number is written backwards

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: Order from a plumbing catalogue to have several delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: The tap is a wiretap on a phone line, not a plumbing fitting. 'sent over' turns NINE into ENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop on a phone line with a bugging device is to do this.
